description:
Advances: ancora.parsing

Severity: Medium (calibrated). Found by the cold auditor on ancora-ayj, not by the critical review.

Problem: lib/ancora/append_only.ex:73-83 authorizes an append-only exception when the ADR affects list names EITHER the requirement id OR the subject id, without checking that the ADR is about the specific change being made. So any accepted ADR whose affects names a subject stands as blanket, indefinite authorization for every future append/requirement_deleted and append/must_downgraded on EVERY requirement in that subject.

Concrete instance created this session: .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md (added by ancora-ayj, correctly, to record the shipped review boundaries) has affects: [ancora.review]. It now authorizes deleting or downgrading any of the ten musts in ancora.review, forever, even though its actual subject matter is the diff granularity of watched cards.

This is the designed mechanism rather than a worker mistake — ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state affects five subjects the same way — but the blast radius is wider than any single ADR needs, and it weakens exactly the guard that exists to make contract erosion visible.

Possible directions (decision needed, none chosen): narrow authorization to requirement ids only, requiring an ADR to name what it authorizes; or keep subject scope but require the ADR to enumerate the requirement ids it covers; or add an expiry/one-shot notion so an ADR authorizes a change once rather than standing open. Each has a cost, and the append-only guard is load-bearing for the whole governance story, so this wants deliberate design rather than a quick patch.

Cannot land on the epic branch: it changes the semantics of the append-only guard, which needs its own ADR and a contract decision about how authorization is scoped.

Ruling needed before code moves (Manuel): how narrowly does an accepted ADR's affects: authorize append-only exceptions? Options in the description: requirement ids only; subject scope but the ADR enumerates the requirement ids it covers; or a one-shot/expiry notion.
Recommended default from the ticket: subject scope stays legal for adr/affects resolution, but append-only AUTHORIZATION requires the ADR to name the requirement id being deleted or downgraded. Existing ADRs that rely on subject scope for authorization get their ids enumerated in the same diff. Record the rule in a new ADR.
Worker: if no comment on this ticket records a ruling when you start, park and ask. Do not choose on Manuel's behalf and do not implement more than one option.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests under ancora.parsing for append-only authorization in test/ancora/append_only_test.exs and affects resolution in test/ancora/decision_parser_test.exs; mix spec.validate on this repo's own corpus stays clean after the rule lands
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) an accepted ADR with affects: [subject] no longer authorizes deleting an unrelated requirement in that subject (append/requirement_deleted still fires); (2) an ADR naming the requirement id does authorize it; (3) this repo's five existing ADRs validate under the new rule, amended in the same diff where needed; (4) the rule is stated as a must in ancora.parsing with clause accounting
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: an ADR authorizes only the deletions and downgrades it names.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/append_only.ex
- lib/ancora/decision_parser.ex, lib/ancora/decision_parser/affects.ex, lib/ancora/schema/decision.ex
- test/ancora/append_only_test.exs, test/ancora/decision_parser_test.exs, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md (substantive must edit with clause accounting)
- .spec/decisions/** (new ADR for the rule; amend existing ADRs' affects: where the new rule requires it)
- priv/spec_init/decisions/**, test/ancora/scaffold/templates_test.exs (decision template guidance)
- docs/migration.md, README.md
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator, correcting an admission defect the cold verifier exposed. ancora.gate.two_append_guards states that an ADR authorizes when affects names the requirement id OR ITS SUBJECT ID, and ancora.gate.scenario.downgrade_authorized_by_adr asserts the subject-only case suppresses the finding. This ticket's rule makes both false. Withholding the file forced the worker to choose between a scope violation and shipping a corpus that contradicts itself, and it chose silently. Substantive edits to that must and that scenario are IN SCOPE and required: the diff that falsifies a requirement fixes it in the same diff.)

- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/gate*
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- lib/ancora/review/**
- lib/mix/tasks/**

Out of Scope (intent):
- no retirement vocabulary here (ancora-n24 builds on this ruling)
- no weakening of append/requirement_deleted or append/must_downgraded defaults

Merge gate:

comments.text: RULING (Manuel, 2026-09-03): Option A. Append-only authorization requires the requirement id in the ADR's affects: list. Subject scope still resolves affects and still satisfies adr/affects checks, but deleting or downgrading requirement X needs X named. Existing ADRs in this repo that rely on subject scope get their requirement ids enumerated in the same diff. Ship with a migration note for Engage and Builder and consider a one-release soft landing on the severity. Record the rule in a new ADR. Coordinate with ancora-n24: a subject id inside retires: covers every requirement under it.
